short: The primary American heavy attack helicopter, designed to destroy enemy armor.
full:
The Hughes AH-64 Apache was introduced in April 1986 to replace the AH-1 Cobra as the primary attack helicopter of the United States Army. Designed to operate day or night and in adverse weather, it featured a nose-mounted sensor suite for target acquisition and night vision, alongside advanced Hellfire anti-tank missiles and a 30mm chain gun linked to the pilot's helmet.

The Apache first saw combat during the 1989 invasion of Panama and played a crucial role in the 1991 Gulf War, where it fired the first shots of the conflict to destroy Iraqi radar networks. It has since become the standard heavy attack helicopter for the US and numerous allied nations, continually upgraded to maintain its anti-armor and close support capabilities.
